title: Mathematical Reasoning and Proof from First Principles
summary: An introductory course in writing and reading rigorous mathematical arguments. Builds from statements, quantifiers, definitions, and proof methods to sets, functions, equivalence relations, induction, infinity, existence/uniqueness, epsilon proofs, and compactness. Designed as a bridge to Analysis, Abstract Algebra, Topology, Discrete Mathematics, and Logic/Type Theory.
assumed_background: basic arithmetic and algebra; familiarity with variables and equations
no prior proof-writing or symbolic logic experience required
lectures 016000-018000 also draw on the real number line and elementary function notation

lectures.title: Claims, logical language, and methods of proof
Sets, functions, quotients, induction, and existence
